The Independent National Electoral Commission will use Saturday’s nationwide mock election to test network connectivity and address potential challenges that could affect the electronic transmission of results during the 2027 general elections. The commission’s Deputy Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Wilfred Ifogah, said the exercise will enable INEC to identify and resolve technical glitches ahead of the general elections. Ifogah, who spoke on Politics Today on Channels Television on Friday, noted that one of the major objectives of the mock poll is to test network capacity for the seamless uploading of results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. He added that the exercise will also help the commission anticipate potential problems that could arise during the elections and fix them before the 2027 polls. “The mock election is important to check the network that will ensure seamless uploads of results on the IReV and tackle issues that may come up during the general elections,” Ifogah said. Speaking on the ballot papers to be used during the exercise, Ifogah stated that they will not represent any political party, stressing that the mock election is strictly for testing electoral technology. He explained that the plain ballot papers will be used to test the ability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System to capture images of the agreed result sheets. It is just plain. We just want to see how the BVAS will capture the photographs of whatever we agreed is going to be the result sheets. So, no party is represented,” he said. On logistics, the INEC official said the commission will replicate the arrangements adopted during the Ekiti and Osun governorship elections. The mock election is expected to test the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections, particularly the deployment of technology for voter accreditation and result management. Also speaking, the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, described the mock election as critical to assessing INEC’s technological readiness, noting that it will be the first nationwide test of the BVAS and IReV since the 2023 general elections. He stated that the exercise will also test the 57,000 BVAS machines procured and tested by the commission, as well as the electronic EC8A result sheets, which will be deployed nationwide for the first time. Itodo noted that the electronic EC8A—previously used in the Federal Capital Territory, Ekiti, and Osun elections—will now be tested on a national scale during the exercise. He added that the mock poll will provide Nigerians with an opportunity to assess INEC’s preparedness and the functionality of the technologies expected to play pivotal roles in the 2027 general elections.
